title.narrative: Rehabilitation of the Beetham Wastewater Stabilization Ponds (WSP) (Trinidad and Tobago)

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

The project aims to reduce pollution from land-based sources, particularly the Beetham Wastewater Stabilisation Ponds, improve ecosystem health, contribute to biodiversity conservation in the Caroni Basin, and reduce marine hypoxia in surrounding coastal ecosystems and the Gulf of Paria, through the implementation of nature-based solutions.

Yes.The Rehabilitation of the Beetham WSP project offers significant socioeconomic benefits at both the national and local levels, contributing to environmental sustainability, public health, economic development, and social equity. These benefits align with the country’s development priorities and international commitments to sustainable development goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation), SDG 14 (Life Below Water), and SDG 15 (Life on Land). National Level Socioeconomic Benefits: Improved Public Health: The rehabilitation of the Beetham WSP will significantly reduce the pollution load from wastewater entering the Caroni River Basin and adjacent coastal ecosystems. The project will help reduce waterborne diseases and improve the population's health by improving wastewater treatment. This will lower healthcare costs related to water contamination, particularly those associated with gastrointestinal diseases and other sanitation-related health issues. Enhanced Economic Growth and Sustainability: The project will contribute to sustainable economic growth by promoting a circular economy approach, where resources (such as nutrients and treated water) can be reused for agricultural and industrial purposes. By recovering nutrients from wastewater and promoting the use of treated water in agriculture and industry, the project will help reduce dependency on imported resources, enhance local agricultural productivity, and increase food security. This contributes to a resilient economy that is less reliant on external imports and more self-sufficient. Attraction of Co-financing and Investments: The project will attract co-financing from international organisations, development banks, and the private sector, providing opportunities for green investments in sustainable infrastructure. These investments will stimulate the green economy, supporting job creation and fostering innovation in sustainable technologies, wastewater treatment, and eco-friendly infrastructure development. Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building: The project will enhance the capacity of national institutions involved in wastewater management, environmental regulation, and public health. This will lead to better policy coherence and stronger governance structures, helping to sustain long-term improvements in environmental and public health management across the country. Support for Achieving International Commitments: The rehabilitation project will help Trinidad and Tobago meet its international environmental commitments, such as those under the Paris Agreement on climate change, the Ramsar Convention on wetlands, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). This will boost the country’s reputation as a leader in environmental sustainability, making it eligible for international funding and partnerships. Local Level Socioeconomic Benefits: Improved Living Conditions: Local communities near the Caroni River Basin will experience improved water quality and reduced pollution. This will lead to a cleaner, healthier environment, reducing the burden of sanitation-related diseases and improving overall quality of life. Job Creation and Livelihoods: The rehabilitation project will create short-term and long-term employment opportunities in construction, waste management, monitoring, and maintenance of the upgraded infrastructure. Local workers will be trained in modern wastewater treatment technologies, creating new skills and knowledge that can be applied to future projects. Developing NbS for wastewater treatment and ecosystem restoration will also create opportunities for local businesses and workers in eco-tourism, agriculture, and environmental services. Gender Empowerment: The project emphasises gender-sensitive approaches, recognising the specific roles that women often play in managing water resources and sanitation. By ensuring women’s active participation in decision-making processes and providing them with training opportunities in sustainable sanitation practices, the project will contribute to gender equality and empowerment. Women, particularly in rural and marginalised areas, will benefit from improved access to clean water and sanitation facilities, enabling them to engage in economic activities, improve their health, and participate more fully in community life. Community Engagement and Social Mobilization: The project’s emphasis on community mobilisation, stakeholder engagement, and awareness raising will foster a sense of ownership and responsibility for local environmental issues. This will lead to greater community participation in environmental stewardship and sustainable waste management practices, ensuring the project's benefits are felt at the grassroots level. Residents will learn about sustainable sanitation practices, which they can apply in their households, helping promote long-term behaviour change that extends beyond the project. Ecosystem Services and Livelihood Enhancement: By restoring coastal ecosystems such as the Caroni Swamp and improving water quality, the project will enhance ecosystem services that local communities depend on, including fisheries, agriculture, and tourism. Cleaner water and restored wetlands will provide better fish and other species habitats, benefiting local fishermen. Additionally, the Caroni River Basin restoration can boost local ecotourism, offering new revenue streams for communities engaged in eco-friendly tourism activities. Enhanced Resilience to Climate Change: The project will improve the resilience of local communities to climate change impacts such as rising sea levels and extreme weather events. Restored wetlands and coastal ecosystems will act as natural buffers, reducing the risk of flooding, erosion, and saltwater intrusion. These improvements will increase the ability of local communities to adapt to the changing climate, protecting their livelihoods and their environments. We confirm that the child project design considers socio-economic benefits to be delivered by the project. These have been clearly described in the Project Description and will be monitored and reported on during project implementation at MTR and Terminal Review.
